title: Edge-break records have no upper bound on depth: a hand-edited project widens the forgiven band

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Follow-up from the review of PR #502 (#303).

`EdgeBreak::is_sane` (`crates/cl/src/cl/edge_break.rs`) and the project loader accept any finite, positive `depth`. The sim's edge-break credit (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/edge_break.rs`) forgives convicted columns down to `edge_z - depth + slope*d`, within the declared plan width. A record hand-edited (or corrupted) to a large depth therefore widens the band in which a real gouge is forgiven. Generated records are bounded by the operation's own parameters, so this only reaches a document through the file.

**Fix:** bound the record at load and in `is_sane`. The depth must not exceed the declaring operation's own chamfer/deburr depth (or a stated absolute cap, e.g. the tool's flute length), and the width must be consistent with the depth and slope. A record outside the bound is dropped by name, the same fail-closed path as a lattice mismatch: the program is then judged against the sharp model.

Done means: a project whose edge-break record states an inflated depth loads with that record dropped and a named note, and the program verdict convicts a cut below the operation's real depth. Pinned by a sim or app test.

Part of #303.

title: UI: pocket/slot recognition entry point (follow-up to #35)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Follow-up to #35, which landed pocket and slot recognition headless: `camcraft_app::recognize::pockets_of` (closed and open pockets, straight slots with open, round or square ends), `recognize::operation_for` (the Pocket or Slot that machines one), and the MCP tool `detect_pockets`. The app has no way to reach it yet.

**Wanted:** a GUI entry point, e.g. a "Detect pockets / slots" action for the selected model (model context menu or the 2D ribbon) that:
- lists the recognised features (kind, floor Z, depth, tightest inside corner, slot width, open sides) and highlights each floor in the viewport when hovered;
- creates the chosen feature's operation through `CreateOperation` with the active tool, one undo step, exactly as `detect_pockets {create}` does - no logic in `ui`, only calls into `app::recognize` (layering ui -> app).

**Done means:** a model with a pocket and a slot shows both in the list, and creating each adds a Pocket / Slot whose parameters page shows the recognised area and depths; Ctrl+Z removes it. Pinned by a `crates/ui/tests` event test.

Part of #35.

title: Slot: a typed Slot whose cutter rides its round cap is convicted of a gouge on every move

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while working #35 (pocket/slot recognition).

**What happens:** a typed 2D Slot whose cutter reaches its round cap is reported as a gouge on every cutting move, with no part model in the document at all, so its path never posts.

**Reproduced on `main` 7e907afa** (headless, app layer): new world, `SetStock` box 80 x 60 x 20, `AddTool` `EM-0600-4FL`, `CreateOperation` Slot on `SrcRef::Stock` with `a = (-15, 0)`, `b = (15, 0)`, `top_z` fixed 20, `bottom_z` fixed 10, stepdown 5, then `GenerateOperation`:
- width 6 (cutter = width, one pass along the centreline): `Gouge` at moves 2, 3, 7, 8, 12, 13 (the plunge and the feed of every level);
- width 10 (rings at +-2): `Gouge` on every feed of every level.

**Likely cause (not confirmed):** the Slot's machining region is `operation::stadium(a, b, width / 2)` with `CAP_SEGMENTS = 16` chords per semicircle, inscribed in the true arc. The tangency law (b) in `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs` wants d(centre, boundary) >= r - tol with `GOUGE_TOL = 0.01`, but a centre on the cap's centre sits only r * cos(5.625 deg) from a chord: 3 mm cutter radius -> 2.9855 < 2.99, a 0.0145 mm "bite" that is pure chord error. The generator's passes ride the true arc, so the verdict convicts a tangent cutter.

**Done means:** a Slot whose passes are tangent to its own stadium verifies clean (no `Gouge`), while a Slot driven past its walls still does; pinned by a test that generates the width-6 and width-10 cases above and asserts no `Gouge`, plus one oversize case that is still convicted.

Related: #35's recognised slots create Slot operations and inherit this until it is fixed (their tests pin the path geometry exactly instead of the verifier's verdict).

title: Fixtures page rows overflow a normal-width properties pane (position, Unmark, Delete and place fields clipped)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Seen by the contributor while testing #482 (#339 slice 4) on a macOS release build (2026-11-09).

**Today:** at a normal properties-pane width, each fixture row on the Fixtures page draws its name, position ("0.00, 0…"), "y" and the Unmark and Delete buttons on one horizontal line, and they clip off the pane's right edge. The "Fixed (does not tu…" checkbox is truncated. The per-fixture `place` row (x y z yaw Apply) has three unlabelled number boxes, and the contributor could not find it. They ended up on the model page, which correctly refuses to move a fixture ("the Fixtures page places it").

**Expected:** the row wraps or stacks so every control is visible at the default pane width. The place fields are labelled X / Y / Z, and the selected fixture's placement is easy to find.

**Done means:** a UI test at the default dock width asserts every fixture row's controls lie inside the pane rect, and the place fields carry axis labels.

title: Pause/Home entries: a Go home as the last entry homes twice (the entry, then the post's own end-of-program home)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Follow-up from #155 (PR #469), from the contributor's hands-on check.

**Today:** with a Go home entry last in the program, the Fanuc post writes `G91 G28 Z0` / `G28 X0 Y0` for the entry, then `G90`, then the same pair again for the post's own end-of-program home before `M30`. The second home is a no-op on the machine, so this is harmless but redundant output.

**Expected:** a trailing Go home entry (no posted op after it) merges with the post's end-of-program home, so it is written once. A Go home between operations stays as it is.

**Done means:** a golden with a trailing Go home shows one home before `M30`. Mid-program homes are unchanged, and Suppress and "Skip pauses and homes" still apply.

title: Wire EDM and Sinker EDM machine types (umbrella - needs breakdown into sub-issues)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

body:
## Summary

Add two new machine kinds to CamCraft, next to `mill`, `lathe` and `mill-turn`:

- `wire_edm`: wire EDM with 2-axis (XY) and 4-axis (XY + UV upper-guide taper) machines.
- `sinker_edm`: sinker / die-sink (ram) EDM with 2-axis and 3-axis machines, and orbit motion.

This is an umbrella. It is not to be worked as one change. Each item in the breakdown below is its own sub-issue, filed only when the umbrella's design is agreed. This issue does not file them.

## Motivation

EDM is the standard route for hardened tool steel, carbide and other materials that are hard to mill. Mould and die shops rely on wire EDM for through-cuts, tapers and punch/die pairs, and on sinker EDM for cavities. CamCraft already plans toolpaths, simulates stock removal and posts G-code for mills and lathes. Extending it to EDM would cover that work, but only if the output is held to the same Prime Directive: a wrong or unverified EDM program is refused by name, never passed through silently.

## Scope

In scope (umbrella):

- Machine kinds `wire_edm` and `sinker_edm`, with `.mch` schema support and a stated `general.kind` (the declaration outranks the axis inventory, as for the existing kinds).
- Wire EDM operations: 2-axis contour, taper contour (constant and variable), 4-axis upper/lower different-profile (ruled surfaces), no-core / pocket burnout, punch/die offset direction, skim passes, tabs/bridges, start hole and threading point, corner strategy.
- Sinker EDM operations: burn to depth with a single electrode, multi-electrode rough and finish with undersize, orbit / vector / planetary patterns, side burning, electrode wear compensation, multiple cavities and positions.
- Electrode generation from part faces (sinker), offset generation with spark gap per pass (wire), ruled-surface pairing (4-axis wire).
- Post processing for at least one ISO-style wire dialect and one sinker dialect, with dialect differences held as data.
- Simulation and verification for both (wire path vs part and slug; electrode collision and depth).
- UI for machine setup and op pages, following the existing op-page pattern.

Out of scope for this umbrella: wire EDM for non-conductive material, small-hole/drilling EDM, EDM generator physics or any model of the spark process itself, and vendor-specific conversational programming.

## Terminology: "4-axis" and "5-axis"

Industry naming is not uniform:

- **4-axis wire EDM** means X, Y for the lower guide and table plus U, V for the upper guide. The upper and lower profiles can differ, so the wire can make a taper or a top-to-bottom profile change. The cut surface is ruled: the straight wire segment between paired upper and lower points sweeps it.
- **5-axis wire EDM** usually means the same four axes plus a separately controlled Z axis (work height or additional 3D positioning). Some vendors use "5-axis" for other things. CamCraft must not infer the count from a label. The `.mch` file states the axes, and the checker reads them.

Sources for this (Makino, Kent, TECHSPEX; see References) describe the layout behaviourally. No vendor definition is copied.

## Machine model

Current state (checked in this repo):

- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` defines `.mch` as JSON with `general.kind` in `mill | lathe | mill-turn`. An unknown kind refuses the file. Axes are the RS-274 letters in `kinematics.default.parts` with travel bands. Absent is not zero: an unstated limit is not judged into existence.
- Crates: `app` (machine checker `crates/app/src/machine`, post mirror), `motion`, `sim`, `post`, `geometry`, `cl`, `tools`.

Proposed additions (to be specified in the schema sub-issue, not decided here):

- `general.kind` gains `wire_edm` and `sinker_edm`. Unknown kinds still refuse.
- Wire EDM keys: UV travel bands (per axis, in mm), upper guide height and lower guide height (distance from the table and from the upper guide to the work top), guide distance (`UV` offset from the lower guide), maximum taper angle (degrees, per side and total), supported wire diameters (list), programmable planes, a wire-tip disposal arm flag, and AWT (automatic wire threading) support as a flag, not a code.
- Sinker EDM keys: Z travel, orbit capability (none, circular, vector, planetary), maximum orbit radius, reference / pickup method, electrode holder limits.
- Power, flushing and condition settings are **user data** in a per-machine table (generator condition number to parameters). They are never copied from a vendor.
- Absent keys are "not stated" and the checker refuses the operation that needs them, by name.

## Operations (wire EDM)

1. **2-axis contour.** Lower-guide XY path. Offset by the wire radius plus spark gap (kerf/2). Lead-in and lead-out. Refuse if no start hole for an enclosed profile.
2. **Taper contour.** Constant taper angle (wire tilted through the part) and variable taper (upper and lower profiles given separately). Refuse if the requested angle exceeds the machine's stated maximum or the UV travel cannot reach it.
3. **4-axis upper/lower profile.** XY and UV move together. The two profiles are paired point by point (CAM chooses the pairing and states it). Ruled-surface check: reject pairings that cross or fold.
4. **No-core / pocket burnout.** Remove the interior of a closed pocket by a series of wire passes. Must state the burnout pattern and the minimum wire clearance to the walls.
5. **Punch vs die.** The same profile offset to the outside (die) or inside (punch) by the kerf, selected by an explicit parameter with a default. Direction is never inferred.
6. **Skim passes.** Rough cut, then one or more skim passes at reduced energy with adjusted offsets. Pass count and offsets are user parameters with defaults.
7. **Tabs / bridges and tab cut-off.** Leave bridges to hold the core or the part; a later pass cuts them. Tab count, width and position are parameters. Refuse if a tab would leave an unsupported slug (see Limitations).
8. **Start hole and threading point.** Enclosed profiles need a start hole (drilled or small-hole). Position is a parameter, and the threading path must be unobstructed through the full height.
9. **Corner strategy.** Minimum internal radius is wire radius plus gap. Corner control (speed/energy reduction at corners) is a parameter. Refuse a corner radius the wire cannot make.

## Operations (sinker EDM)

1. **Burn to depth (single electrode).** Depth from a stated datum (workpiece top, cavity floor or electrode tip). Electrode length and offset from the pickup.
2. **Rough and finish with undersize.** Rough electrode with a larger undersize, finish electrode with a smaller one. Undersize per side is a parameter with a default. Warn if the finish electrode is not smaller than the rough.
3. **Orbit patterns.** Circular, vector and planetary, as the machine states them. Orbit radius is a parameter. The pattern name is data, not a CamCraft constant. Refuse an orbit the machine does not state.
4. **Side burning.** Burn of walls by lateral movement. Stated as a separate op with its own undersize.
5. **Electrode wear compensation.** Axial wear compensated in Z. Compensation is estimated from a stated rate or measured between layers. Never assume a fixed ratio.
6. **Multiple cavities / positions.** Several positions from one electrode, each with its own reference.
7. **Electrode generation from part faces.** Derive the electrode shape from the part faces, offset by undersize and orbit. Refuse degenerate or self-intersecting results.

## Geometry and CAM engine needs

- Offsetting with spark gap per pass. Each skim has its own offset. The offset is computed from the wire diameter plus the gap in the condition table, not hard-coded.
- Ruled-surface pairing for 4-axis wire. Pairing rules are explicit and checked for crossings and folds.
- Sync points between upper and lower profiles (matching point counts or a stated mapping).
- Slug and core analysis: which region of an internal profile will be free to move when cut through.
- Electrode shape from a 3D face set. Undersize and orbit envelopes. Degenerate input (zero-area faces, self-intersections) errors cleanly.

## Post processing

- Dialects are held as data and documented per machine, not copied from any vendor post. CamCraft's own `.cps` engine is used, with the same provenance comment law as the existing posts.
- Wire needs: wire compensation codes (G41/G42 in the controller's dialect, with the offset written as a machine-stated value), taper or UV move codes, AWT or threading code (M-code as data), wire-tip disposal (M-code as data), skim and condition codes (as data, not vendor values).
- Sinker needs: depth and orbit codes, electrode-change codes (if any), reference/pickup words.
- Refuse by name when a required code is not stated for the machine's dialect. Never silently drop a line.
- Research shows wire EDM dialects differ widely. G41/G42 mean left/right compensation in one control and are not guaranteed to map to kerf offset in another. G21/G22 are units and travel limit in one control, not taper. Each dialect's meaning is therefore taken from the user's controller manual, not from a generic table.

## Simulation and verification

- Wire: 2D sweep of the wire path (lower and upper), with the taper's ruled surface. Check against the part (gouge), the slug (collision and drop), and the work height.
- Taper: check the computed angle against the machine maximum and the UV travel.
- Sinker: electrode collision with the part, the electrode's depth against the datum, and the electrode's clearance during orbit.
- Both: flagged unsafe moves block the post (Prime Directive). A flag is never passed silently.

## Limitations and refusals (must be implemented)

- Taper angle above the machine's stated maximum: refuse, name the op and the angle.
- UV unreachable (outside travel or outside the guide distance): refuse.
- Enclosed profile without a start hole: refuse.
- Unsupported dialect or missing required code: refuse, name the code.
- Missing wire diameter, gap or condition: refuse at command creation, not in the generator.
- Corner radius below the wire-plus-gap minimum: refuse.
- Slug that can move into the wire or be dropped uncontrolled: refuse unless a tab or capture is set.
- Electrode undersize not smaller than the finished cavity, or orbit radius above the machine's: refuse.
- Degenerate geometry (zero-area, self-intersecting, nonsense tolerance): clean error, never a panic. No `unwrap()` or `expect()` (AGENTS.md).

## UI

- Machine setup: the new kinds and their keys, with absent values shown as "not stated".
- Op pages: wire op pages and sinker op pages in the existing op-page tab pattern. Parameters are commands (Everything Is a Command): changes go through the command history.

## Clean-room note

- References are limited to public manufacturer documentation and handbooks, public standards (RS-274, ISO 6983), research papers and our own design notes.
- No vendor post processor, template, dialect file or machine definition is read, adapted or copied. Dialect behaviour comes from the user's controller manual, supplied by the user, and is recorded as data.
- New EDM algorithms (ruled-surface pairing, orbit compensation) are written from published technical literature.
- Each new module carries a one-line provenance comment naming its public source.

## Proposed sub-issue breakdown

Each line is a future sub-issue, filed when the umbrella is agreed. They are not filed by this issue.

- [ ] Machine kinds `wire_edm` and `sinker_edm` + `.mch` schema (wire: UV travel, guides, max taper, wire diameters; sinker: orbit capability, Z travel, reference)
- [ ] Condition/power table as user data (generator condition to parameters), with absent-is-not-zero refusals
- [ ] Wire 2-axis contour op (offset by wire radius + gap, lead-in/out, start-hole check)
- [ ] Wire taper contour op (constant angle, max-angle and UV-reach refusals)
- [ ] Wire 4-axis upper/lower op (ruled-surface pairing, crossing/fold checks)
- [ ] Wire skim passes (per-pass offset, reduced-energy condition per pass)
- [ ] Wire tabs / bridges + tab cut-off, slug analysis
- [ ] Wire no-core / pocket burnout op
- [ ] Wire punch vs die offset direction parameter
- [ ] Wire corner strategy + minimum-radius refusal
- [ ] Wire EDM post (ISO-style dialect, data-driven codes, refusal on missing codes)
- [ ] Wire EDM simulation / verification (wire path vs part, slug, taper limit)
- [ ] Sinker burn-to-depth op (datum, electrode length, pickup)
- [ ] Sinker rough/finish with undersize (multi-electrode, finish-smaller check)
- [ ] Sinker orbit patterns (circular, vector, planetary as stated by the machine)
- [ ] Sinker side burning op
- [ ] Sinker electrode wear compensation (estimated rate and measured layers)
- [ ] Sinker electrode generation from part faces (degenerate-input errors)
- [ ] Sinker EDM post (depth, orbit and pickup words as data)
- [ ] Sinker EDM simulation (electrode collision, depth, orbit clearance)
- [ ] UI: machine setup pages and wire/sinker op pages in the op-page tab pattern

## Done means

Every sub-issue above is filed and closed, and the umbrella is closed with the last one. Each closed sub-issue has a pinned test and a golden output where it posts code.

## References

Publicly available sources, found while researching this issue. Used for behaviour and terminology only.

- Makino, EDM wire tutorial (4/5-axis wire, upper and lower guide, UV layout): https://www.makino.com/resources/content-library/article/archive/edm-wire-tutorial/198
- Kent USA, WSi-200 operation manual (public PDF, UV and taper behaviour): https://kentusa.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/Kent-USA-WSi-200-OPERATION-2018.pdf
- TECHSPEX, guide to buying a wire EDM (axis terminology): https://www.techspex.com/kc/guide-to-buying-machine-tools/buying-a-wire-edm
- Manufacturing Processes, EDM (start holes, skims, kerf, corner radius): https://manufacturingprocesses.org/processes/cutting/electrical-discharge-machining
- Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering, comprehensive review of wire EDM (2024): https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/mechanical-engineering/articles/10.3389/fmech.2024.1322605/full
- Methods and variables in EDM, review (wire diameter, kerf, spark gap): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7736727/
- Xingineer, wire EDM design guide: start holes and corners: https://www.xingineer.com/wire-edm-design-guide-start-holes-and-corners/
- Corner accuracy study, WEDM of AISI D2 (Springer, 2025): https://www.link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00170-025-15998-7
- Autodesk FeatureCAM documentation, XYUV wire EDM output (behaviour only): https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/FCAM-XBUILD/files/GUID-0ADDCB82-00DA-4212-80FF-D530A6113479.htm
- Sodick LN1W/LN2W control manual (public PDF, example of dialect differences only): https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content//tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf
- Sinker EDM orbit: cavity dimensional error and non-uniform electrode compensation: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0890695505000325
- Sinker EDM orbit: profile deviation and compensation in orbital EDM (Springer): https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00170-019-03601-9
- Electrode wear compensation in contour EDM: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0890695504001269
- Electrode wear compensation in planetary EDM: http://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11740-017-0778-8
- Reliability of electrode wear compensation based on material removal (DTU): https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/reliability-of-electrode-wear-compensation-based-on-material-remo/
- RS-274 and ISO 6983 (G-code standards, behaviour of G41/G42 and axis lettering).

Research gaps, noted for the design sub-issues: no manufacturer-validated tab dimensions, no universal AWT or slug-retention procedure, and no universal orbit terminology. These must come from the user's machine manual when the sub-issues are specced.
